description: ol-var-not-visible (issue #825): spec/execution-model.md:431-447's own worked example, verbatim. `draw_steps` cannot see the top-level `:count`, because inside a procedure body exactly three things are visible — its parameters, the bindings its body has already made, and names declared `global` (spec/execution-model.md:389-394). The diagnostic fires on the READ, `forward :count * 10`, because the read comes first; had the write come first it would have created a binding in the scope where the write appears — the `repeat` body, born fresh on every turn — which is a genuinely different variable and correctly silent. The second finding is the read inside the write's own value, `:count + 1`, which fails for the same reason; the assignment TARGET is never reported. Params carry both `name` and `procedure`, which is what a generic `ol-undefined-var` could not express. This fixture asserts code, span, params and stage; it does NOT assert the message, because the harness compares prose only under `compareMessages` — the two normative prose requirements of spec/error-model.md:132 (name the boundary, name the fix) are asserted in packages/parser/src/variable-visibility.test.mjs and packages/runtime/src/checker-runtime-agreement.test.mjs, the latter byte-for-byte against the runtime. tests/conformance/core-language/scoping/procedure-boundary-hides-a-top-level-read runs the same program, so one source is pinned at both the check and the run stage.
